title: ByteDance in Talks to Secure MediaTek AI Chips for Data Centers
key_facts: Bloomberg reported ByteDance is close to a deal to buy custom AI chips (ASICs) from Taiwan's MediaTek for its data centres.
ASICs are chips designed for particular computing tasks; MediaTek is a major vendor for Google's tensor processing units.
ByteDance agreed earlier this year to buy millions of AI chips from Qualcomm.
Bloomberg reported ByteDance is considering capital spending of up to $70 billion this year, more than double last year.
MediaTek expects AI-chip sales of about $2 billion this year and targets 15% of an $80 billion market next year, per Bloomberg.
Chip stocks fell on Thursday; Kospi dropped more than 7%.
quote_evidence: MediaTek would supply ByteDance with application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs), which are designed for particular computing tasks.
Bloomberg reported that ByteDance is considering capital expenditure of up to $70 billion this year, more than double last year’s total, as it builds out its AI infrastructure.
why_it_matters_hint: A custom-chip deal would give MediaTek a bigger foothold against Broadcom and could shift ByteDance demand away from Nvidia GPUs.
notes: Bloomberg blocked by bot wall; read Stocktwits copy on TradingView. Reuters headline says ByteDance "nears" a deal; nothing signed is reported.
